newsitem.title: CANADA: Great Lakes ship engineers expected to ratify deal.
newsitem.headline: Great Lakes ship engineers expected to ratify deal.

text.p: Shipboard engineers were expected to ratify a tentative agreement on a labour contract signed between three shippers and the Canadian Marine Officers Union, one of the negotiators said Tuesday.

"Absolutely, it's going along with (ratification) recommendations to the union membership," grain handler and shipper Parrish & Heimbecker Ltd personel manager Coral Milne said from the St. Catharines, Ont., office.
CMOU members who navigate for the Canadian Lake Carriers' Association went on strike at 0800 CST Thursday and returned to work Sunday.
The CLCA includes P&H, Algoma Central Marine and N.M. Paterson & Sons Ltd.
"All the (shipboard) engineers are back on the job now," Algoma's Al Vanagas said in an interview from St. Catharines.
CMOU officials were not immediately available for comment.
Navigation on the Great Lakes should resume April 2 when the St. Lawrence Seaway is scheduled to open for the 1997 season, Vanagas and Milne said.
The strike affected 23 ships owned by Algoma, seven lakers owned by N.M. Paterson & Sons Ltd and Parrish & Heimbecker Ltd, they said.
CMOU president Richard Vezina was outside the Montreal head office on unrelated negotiation, union officials said.
